clue.text: Just the place to try to get money from the horses

parts.note: to dun someone is to press them persistently for payment of a debt
a stable is a set of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer

explanation.surface: A punter thinks the racecourse is just the spot to win some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNSTABLE is a town in Bedfordshire, England. 'Just the' only leads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunstable is an English town, so it is a named location.

clue.text: Formerly tuppence a trip? An outrage — it was only worth three ha'pence

definitions.text: Formerly tuppence a trip? An outrage — it was only worth three ha'pence

parts.words: Formerly tuppence a trip? An outrage — it was only worth three ha'pence
parts.note: a mock complaint about an old fare of two pennies for a ride, when the small old English silver coin named here was valued at just one and a half pence

explanation.surface: A passenger grumbles about a pre-decimal fare, insisting the journey was worth far less.
explanation.walkthrough: Pre-decimal British money had pennies and halfpennies (ha'pence); the clue describes an obsolete sixteenth-century coin worth three halfpence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word named a small old coin valued at a penny-ha'penny, the sum the clue mentions.

clue.text: Terrible rain at a point in the Highlands

indicators.note: terrible weather has the letters of rain thrown into disorder

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Dreadful downpours strike somewhere in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' turns RAIN into NAIR; NAIRN is a town on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a town found in the Highland region of Scotland.

clue.text: Speculate about article on zero inflation

parts.note: the definite article in English
O looks like the figure nought
inflation is a rise in prices

explanation.surface: An economist muses over a piece about inflation falling to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to form ideas or hypotheses, which is what theorising means.

clue.text: Grace's happy event

explanation.surface: Someone named Grace has had a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a woman's name, but here it is the prayer said before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grace before meals asks for divine favour, and a welcome stroke of good luck, often a new baby, is also called this.

clue.text: Some of René Clair's lightest confections

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but the answer is one example of such airy pastries

indicators.note: only part of the letters of the film director's name is taken

explanation.surface: Praise for the French film director René Clair's most delicate works.
explanation.walkthrough: René Clair was a French film director; 'confections' sounds like his films but means pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger filled with cream is about as airy a sweet treat as exists.

clue.text: Many sheets of paper required for an illusion

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
a ream is a quantity of paper, usually 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A stationer insists a big stack of paper is needed to create a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy or vision that is not real is a kind of illusion.

clue.text: Wizard American lawyer begins to cause expense

indicators.note: the lawyer comes at the start, ahead of the wizard

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor
a mage is a magician

explanation.surface: A sorcerer's attorney starts running up costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' in 'what's the damage?' is slang for cost; 'to cause' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the cost of something is asked about as 'what's the damage?'.

clue.text: Able, perhaps, to make speech complicated

indicators.note: suggests the letters of able might be arranged another way

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a formal speech

explanation.surface: A capable person makes a speech overly intricate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ABLE into ELAB, then ORATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detailed and intricate is complicated.

clue.text: Note boy raised in the anthem

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters are read upwards, so the whole pair is turned backwards

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
Tom is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A choirboy holds up his note during the anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TE + TOM into MOTET, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral piece, as an anthem is.

clue.text: Inexperience causes sloth in the medley event

indicators.note: the animal is placed inside the jumbled letters
a medley is a mixture, so the letters of event are mixed up

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: A slow swimmer in the medley race shows a lack of experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' jumbles EVENT into NEVTE, and 'in' puts AI inside it. The medley event looks like a swimming race.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence born of lack of worldly experience.

clue.text: Essayist finds a way to criticize

parts.note: Charles Lamb was an English essayist, author of the Essays of Elia
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: A writer discovers a means of attacking others.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to attack verbally and harshly, i.e. to criticize.

clue.text: This red is nearly gold

parts.note: on an archery target the gold bull is ringed by a red band, the circle just outside the centre

explanation.surface: Something reddish is almost golden in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery the target's central gold is surrounded by red rings; the ring next to the bull is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring adjoining the bull on a target is the one closest to the middle.

clue.text: Music lighter, perhaps, for a fairground attraction

parts.note: swing is a style of jazz music
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge, one kind of vessel

explanation.surface: A fairground ride accompanied by music and lit up brighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' suggests a cigarette lighter or brightness, but it is a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A swingboat is a boat-shaped swing ride found at fairs.

clue.text: Lying about assuming an attitude

parts.note: re means concerning
posing is adopting a posture

explanation.surface: Someone is telling lies about putting on a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths but means resting.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down at rest is to repose.

clue.text: I, for instance, may go to church to pass judgment

parts.note: the word I is an example of a personal pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone might attend church in order to deliver a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare formally, as a judge declares a verdict.

clue.text: Prohibited, say, from having a slice of bacon

indicators.note: signals that a word is pronounced like another

parts.note: barred means banned

explanation.surface: Someone is banned from eating a rasher of bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: BARRED sounds like BARD, a thin strip of fat bacon laid over meat when roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cookery the term names a strip of fat or bacon tied over lean meat.

clue.text: Mess of dried sage proved unsatisfactory

indicators.note: a mess implies the letters of dried sage are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook's mess of dried herbs turned out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Food that 'disagreed' with you did not suit your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that disagrees with someone upsets them, so it proved unsuitable.

clue.text: Side getting together for motor sport

explanation.surface: A team gathers to take part in motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A team regrouping is said to be recovering and gathering; the motor sport is road racing on public roads in stages.

clue.text: Plato — his disorder might have been cured here!

definitions.text: Plato — his disorder might have been cured here!

indicators.note: disorder implies the letters of Plato and his are scrambled

explanation.surface: The Greek philosopher's ailment could have been treated somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges PLATO HIS; the whole clue also describes the place where an illness would be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is an institution where the sick are treated.

clue.text: Warning to look both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Advice to check left and right before crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A short blast on a car horn alerts others to danger.

clue.text: Titled lady found in pubs that accept singles

indicators.note: the pubs take in the singles, holding them inside

parts.note: bars are pubs
ones are single units

explanation.surface: A peeress turns up in bars that welcome unmarried people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singles' looks like unattached people, but means ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness holds a noble rank, so she is a lady with a title.

clue.text: The woman's tolerant, not having a dissenting view

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: means the letter a is removed from the word

parts.note: easy-going, so easy

explanation.surface: She is broad-minded and lacks any contrary opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having a' drops the A from EASY, leaving ESY.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief opposed to orthodox doctrine.

clue.text: Tom caught sight of note in your keeping

parts.note: saw means spotted

indicators.note: the abbreviation for your holds the note inside

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Tom spotted a message you were holding.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero; 'note' looks like a message but is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the famous fictional boy, so the surname completes the first name.

clue.text: Field boundary perhaps and play defensively

explanation.surface: Marking a field's edge and batting cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to stonewall is to bat purely defensively.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry-stone wall can divide fields; in cricket, to stonewall is to block without scoring.

clue.text: Foreigner escaping from Belsen or Auschwitz

indicators.note: the word gets out from inside the place names

explanation.surface: A foreign prisoner flees a wartime concentration camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Senor is the Spanish title for a man, so to an English speaker it suggests a foreign gentleman.

clue.text: One animal is about the same as another

definitions.text: One animal is about the same as another

parts.words: One animal is about the same as another
parts.note: a stray Asian village dog whose name is just a variant spelling of another name for the same creature, the pye-dog

explanation.surface: A naturalist remarks that two creatures are nearly identical.
explanation.walkthrough: The pi-dog and pye-dog are one animal, a half-wild Indian stray, under two spellings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling naming the ownerless scavenging dog of Asian towns.

clue.text: Put off diet at first by relative

indicators.note: only the opening letter of diet is used

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member discourages someone from dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt is to discourage or intimidate.

clue.text: "Get thee to a" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Hamlet's words to Ophelia, telling her to go to a convent

explanation.surface: A famous line from Shakespeare's Hamlet with its last word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet tells Ophelia to enter a convent, the house where religious sisters live.

clue.text: Butt in with one no-trump cheeky!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no-trump
rude means impudent

explanation.surface: A bridge player interrupts by bidding no-trump impudently.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to interfere uninvited, to intrude.

clue.text: Thin film — director unknown

parts.note: Carol Reed was the British director of The Third Man
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A slight movie whose director is anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin film' looks like a single phrase; 'Thin' is the definition and 'film director' is Reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means slender like a reed stalk.

clue.text: Directed characters in great duel

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of great duel are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone orchestrated the roles in a big fight scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to control or govern, so directed matches regulated.
